action.description: Add a vitamin C-rich food in the same meal
action.engine_instruction: Pair beans, lentils, tofu, fortified grains, or greens with citrus, peppers, berries, tomato, or broccoli.

evidence.summary: Human absorption research and NIH guidance identify vitamin C as an enhancer of nonheme iron absorption.

sources.title: Iron: Fact Sheet for Health Professionals

action.description: Include a modest amount of fat in the meal
action.engine_instruction: Add olive oil, avocado, nuts, seeds, tahini, or another compatible fat to salads/vegetables.

evidence.summary: Randomized meal studies show substantially higher carotenoid absorption when vegetables are consumed with fat.

sources.title: Carotenoid absorption from salad and the effect of salad dressing fat

action.description: Consume with a meal containing fat
action.engine_instruction: For vitamin D-fortified or naturally rich meals, retain a compatible fat source.

evidence.summary: Randomized human studies show higher vitamin D absorption with fat-containing meals.

sources.title: Dietary fat increases vitamin D-3 absorption

action.description: Include fat in the same meal
action.engine_instruction: Pair squash, sweet potato, carrots, or greens with a modest fat source.

evidence.summary: NIH and human feeding studies support fat-dependent absorption of carotenoids and vitamin A.

sources.title: Vitamin A and Carotenoids: Fact Sheet for Health Professionals

rule_name: Complete limiting amino acids across the day

action.description: Combine or rotate complementary plant proteins
action.engine_instruction: Recommend culturally appropriate combinations such as beans with rice or hummus with whole-grain bread.

evidence.summary: Protein-quality guidance supports complementary patterns while rejecting the need for rigid same-meal combining.

sources.title: Dietary protein quality evaluation in human nutrition

rule_name: Lemon or acid with nonheme iron

action.description: Use a vitamin C-containing acidic ingredient
action.engine_instruction: Use lemon/lime, tomato, or vitamin C-rich peppers; do not code generic vinegar as equivalent to vitamin C.

evidence.summary: Human iron-absorption evidence supports ascorbic acid; this rule prevents an overly broad acid heuristic.

sources.title: Iron: Fact Sheet for Health Professionals

rule_name: Lactose and vitamin D support calcium use

action.description: Prefer calcium foods with adequate vitamin D status; retain lactose if tolerated
action.engine_instruction: For calcium optimization, pair with vitamin D-fortified choices when compatible.

evidence.summary: NIH evidence summary describes vitamin D-dependent calcium absorption.

sources.title: Calcium: Fact Sheet for Health Professionals
